In 2024, Wout van Aert dominated a reduced bunch sprint to take the 2nd of his 3 stage wins that year. Sepp Kuss was essential to propel him to the victory. Pau Miquel was 3rd.
On both occasions, Cordoba witnessed thrilling racing as late attackers were reeled in just before the finish. It was a similar scenario when John Degenkoilb won in Cordoba in La Vuelta 14.
The last attacker to win a La Vuelta stage in Cordoba was Peter Sagan in 2011. In his maiden Grand Tour, the young Slovak (21 years old at the time) raced for Liquigas-Cannondale and he participated in a team attack with Vincenzo Nibali, Valerio Agnoli and Eros Capecchi that only Movistar’s Pablo Lastras followed. Sagan eventually took the first of his 18 Grand Tour stage wins.
All the aforementioned stages to Cordoba featured the Alto del 14% in the finale. The most emblematic rider from the area is Antonio Gomez del Moral (from Cabra, 75 km south of Cordoba), the winner of three La Vuelta stages, including stage 9 of the 1962 edition with a finish in Cordoba.

The most emblematic rider from the area is Antonio Gomez del Moral (from Cabra, 75 km south of Cordoba), the winner of three La Vuelta stages, including stage 9 of the 1962 edition with a finish in Cordoba.
The future of Andalusian cycling could be defined by Diego Lopez, who was born in Estepona in 2008 and won today the 50th edition of the GP Rüebliland, a staple of the junior calendar. Léo Bisiaux won it in 2023, and Lennard Kämna in 2014.

There are three Andalusian riders in the peloton of La Vuelta 26 (Carlos Rodriguez, Cristian Rodriguez, José Manuel Diaz Gallego) but none of them is from the province of Cordoba. The most emblematic rider from the area is Antonio Gomez del Moral (from Cabra, 75 km south of Cordoba), the winner of three La Vuelta stages, including stage 9 of the 1962 edition with a finish in Cordoba.
The future of Andalusian cycling could be defined by Diego Lopez, who was born in Estepona in 2008 and won today the 50th edition of the GP Rüebliland, a staple of the junior calendar. Léo Bisiaux won it in 2023, and Lennard Kämna in 2014.

In 2024, Wout van Aert dominated a reduced bunch sprint to take the 2nd of his 3 stage wins that year. Sepp Kuss was essential to propel him to the victory. Pau Miquel was 3rd.
On both occasions, Cordoba witnessed thrilling racing as late attackers were reeled in just before the finish. It was a similar scenario when John Degenkoilb won in Cordoba in La Vuelta 14.
The last attacker to win a La Vuelta stage in Cordoba was Peter Sagan in 2011. In his maiden Grand Tour, the young Slovak (21 years old at the time) raced for Liquigas-Cannondale and he participated in a team attack with Vincenzo Nibali, Valerio Agnoli and Eros Capecchi that only Movistar’s Pablo Lastras followed. In 2024, Wout van Aert dominated a reduced bunch sprint to take the 2nd of his 3 stage wins that year. Sepp Kuss was essential to propel him to the victory. Pau Miquel was 3rd.

In 2024, Wout van Aert dominated a reduced bunch sprint to take the 2nd of his 3 stage wins that year. Sepp Kuss was essential to propel him to the victory. Pau Miquel was 3rd.
On both occasions, Cordoba witnessed thrilling racing as late attackers were reeled in just before the finish. It was a similar scenario when John Degenkoilb won in Cordoba in La Vuelta 14.
The last attacker to win a La Vuelta stage in Cordoba was Peter Sagan in 2011. In his maiden Grand Tour, the young Slovak (21 years old at the time) raced for Liquigas-Cannondale and he participated in a team attack with Vincenzo Nibali, Valerio Agnoli and Eros Capecchi that only Movistar’s Pablo Lastras followed. There are three Andalusian riders in the peloton of La Vuelta 26 (Carlos Rodriguez, Cristian Rodriguez, José Manuel Diaz Gallego) but none of them is from the province of Cordoba. The most emblematic rider from the area is Antonio Gomez del Moral (from Cabra, 75 km south of Cordoba), the winner of three La Vuelta stages, including stage 9 of the 1962 edition with a finish in Cordoba.
The future of Andalusian cycling could be defined by Diego Lopez, who was born in Estepona in 2008 and won today the 50th edition of the GP Rüebliland, a staple of the junior calendar. Léo Bisiaux won it in 2023, and Lennard Kämna in 2014.
